topics.topic: Ownership and ordering of listener read-timeout installation
questions: Which module capability imports LISTENER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and applies it to each owner-interface and service-API listener or accepted connection?
Which capability opens each listener and imports and installs `LISTENER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, and does it install the timeout on both surfaces before either can accept a connection?
Which module imports LISTENER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, which capability applies it to each listener or accepted connection, and who calls that capability?

quotes:
In order: `configuration.load_configuration`;
`backups.probe_backup_location`; `store.open_store`; the owner interface's
listener and then, unless the start is owner-only, the service API's, each
at its address in the loaded configuration (A17 rule 1); then the surfaces answer; then two
passes: `owner_sessions.end_expired_sessions` every imported
`SESSION_PASS_SECONDS` and, except in an owner-only start,
`backups.run_daily_backup_if_due` every imported `BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS`, each
from the start as Conventions, "Passes", says.

`instance_lifecycle`'s two listeners share one HTTP implementation. Each
connection's socket waits at most the imported
`LISTENER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (30) for the next bytes of a request — its
headers or its body, an upload's head and file among them; a wait that
reaches it ends the stream with a failure, which the reader sees as any
stream failure: an upload's head then gives no CSRF value (refused at stage
(1)), its file part `file_unreadable`, and the connection is closed.
judgement.why: State 5 assigns listener opening to `instance_lifecycle.start_instance`, and State 6 assigns the imported timeout to `instance_lifecycle`'s shared HTTP implementation for every connection on both listeners.

topics.topic: Read-timeout failure outcome, response, diagnostics, and upload cleanup
questions: When LISTENER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS expires while a request is being read, what flow outcome follows besides closing the connection, particularly for an upload already admitted after its head was read?

When the listener read timeout expires after the upload head passed session and CSRF checks but while the file stream is being read, is this the stated unreadable-file refusal, or a transport close with no refusal answer; and in either case what cleanup completes before the connection closes?

When the read timeout expires, is the connection closed unanswered before any route capability is called, or is the partial request delivered as a read failure to the surface or upload flow; and is any diagnostic produced?

quotes:
`instance_lifecycle`'s two listeners share one HTTP implementation. Each
connection's socket waits at most the imported
`LISTENER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (30) for the next bytes of a request — its
headers or its body, an upload's head and file among them; a wait that
reaches it ends the stream with a failure, which the reader sees as any
stream failure: an upload's head then gives no CSRF value (refused at stage
(1)), its file part `file_unreadable`, and the connection is closed. A
request answered before its body was read to its framed end — any request,
not an upload alone — has the remainder discarded unread and its
connection closed; a connection carries a next request only after one whose
body was read to its end.

No refusal
carries a digest: a file over the size limit is refused before any of it is
parsed — a declared length over it before any byte is read, otherwise as
soon as more than it has been read; a stream that fails or ends before its
declared length is refused as `file_unreadable`, replacing nothing kept and
changing nothing of the session but the instant of its last request, which
every request carrying it moves (A13 rule 2) — and an
unreadable or malformed one is refused with its kind alone.

After an upload's answer, whatever it was — accepted, or refused before any
or after some bytes were read — `owner_interface` discards the unread
remainder of the body without reading it into anything and closes the
connection its listener accepted; a connection that carried an upload is
never reused.
judgement.why: State 6 makes timeout expiry a stream failure: during the head it yields a stage-(1) refusal, during the file it yields `file_unreadable` without replacing the kept upload, and the upload connection is then closed after unread-body cleanup.

topics.topic: Read-timeout start, reset, queue accounting, and wait ownership
questions: When does the timeout begin, what receipt resets it, and does time spent waiting in the listener queue count?

Which module and capability own the wait, reset its timer when bytes arrive, and close the connection when it expires: `instance_lifecycle`, `service_api` or `owner_interface`, or a deterministic transport backend called by them?
